column1: # passB.tsv -- blind transcription pass B, rah-canada-1869 (RAH 9/6958, Leg. XIX no 117/2-3)
# Read from images/10137302.jpg (p302) and images/10137303.jpg (p303), cross-checked against
# 3x-enlarged, autocontrast crops of each cipher line made from the per-line crop files in
# images/ (p302_L##.jpg, p303_L##.jpg) via a local PIL script (not committed, scratchpad only).
# Interpretive symbol choices made consistently through this pass, for the reconciler to check
#  - a plain vertical stroke with small top/bottom serifs (looks like a capital "I") -> digit 1
#  - the flag/gamma-shaped hook (horizontal top stroke + vertical/diagonal down-stroke, distinct
#    from [hook] below) -> read as digit 1 (an alternate cursive form); genuinely possible this is
#    a "7" instead -- flagged here as the single most uncertain recurring glyph in this pass.
#  - the long horizontal stroke ending in an upward hook/flick at its right end (arrow-like "->") -> [hook]
#  - small single-hump loop, very common as last character of a token -> [loopn]
#  - taller ascender flourish, common as first character of a token -> [bigloop]
#  - open oval immediately inside a run of digits -> digit 0; an open oval standing on its own
#    (not obviously part of a digit run) -> [circle], per the atlas's own caution that this pair
#  - small closed circle with a visible interior dot/bar -> [circledot]
#  - a curling-tailed mark resembling a handwritten "?" (seen a handful of times) -> read as digit 9;
#  - "." "," "-" transcribed literally where they read as ordinary punctuation/separators between
#    groups; a longer isolated horizontal stroke that looks like part of a symbol rather than a
# No new [gNN] glyphs were needed; every non-digit mark seen matched a label already in atlas.md.
# Many individual glyph calls in this pass are uncertain (marked informally above); this is a
# blind pass for tools/reconcile_passes.py to compare against an independent pass B... reading.
